title: Community
hook: a group to pray or talk with
tomorrow: who do you ask when you can't tell God's voice from your own?

segments.voice: Yesterday: take up and read, and the line keep learning. A book is something you can carry alone. Today's piece isn't.

So who do you call when the faith gets lonely? Start with an odd detail in Matthew. Jesus tells his listeners to pray by themselves, in the Douay-Rheims: "enter into thy chamber, and having shut the door, pray to thy Father in secret." A few lines later, he gives them the words to pray in that shut room. Look for an I in them, or a my. There isn't one. Our Father. Give us. Forgive us. Deliver us. Why hand someone a plural prayer for a room with the door closed?
screen: `PRAY BEHIND A SHUT DOOR.` → `NO I, NO MY.` → `WHY A PLURAL PRAYER?`

segments.voice: Here's the answer the prayer gives: in it, nobody is ever only one. Even alone, behind a shut door, the one praying says our, and stands inside a family. Catholics put it this way: faith is personal, but never private. The first Christians lived it out in public. Acts says they "were persevering in the doctrine of the apostles, and in the communication of the breaking of bread, and in prayers." Teaching, sharing, the bread, the prayers, and all of it together. One word to tell a friend: persevering. These weren't people who came once for a big event. They kept showing up. Then Jesus makes a promise about small groups, not stadiums: "where there are two or three gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them." Two or three is enough. So a rule for life needs a few people, not a crowd: a parish Bible study, a young adult group, a few neighbors who pray the rosary, two friends who talk honestly about God over tacos. People who'll notice when you stop coming, and ask.
screen: `OUR FATHER, BEHIND A SHUT DOOR.` · `PERSONAL, NEVER PRIVATE.` · `THEY KEPT SHOWING UP.` · `TWO OR THREE IS ENOUGH.` · then, large: `NOT ALONE.`

segments.voice: Pick up your phone and think of two people who might pray, read or just talk faith with you: a friend, a cousin, someone from the parish. Send one of them a short message asking if they'd want to meet once. Then sit with the word our, and the faces it holds for you.
Community. Two or three gathered, persevering together, praying a prayer that says our even behind a closed door.
Keep this one close: not alone, since even the shut-door prayer begins with our. Until tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1738 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: WHO DO YOU ASK WHEN YOU CAN'T TELL GOD'S VOICE FROM YOUR OWN?`

howItsDone: Catholics find community in their parish and in smaller groups within it: Bible studies, prayer groups, young adult groups, rosary groups and campus ministries.

fork.setup: you've joined a parish Bible study. after three weeks, one member is great, one talks too much, one never speaks. what does Acts suggest?
options: keep showing up. the first Christians persevered with each other, not with perfect people.
look for a better group whose people fit you right away.
stop going and pray the Our Father alone; it's the same prayer.
fork.reveal: Acts calls them persevering. the point of two or three isn't a perfect fit; it's people who keep coming back.

original.note: Greek: sharing, fellowship. the word in Acts 2:42 the Douay-Rheims renders the communication.

trapdoor: what you thought: faith is just between me and God.
what it means: personal, never private; even the shut-door prayer says our.
what a scholar hears: Acts 2:42 names koinonia, sharing, beside the breaking of bread and the prayers; the Our Father in Matthew 6:9–13 never says I or my.
guess: a few people who pray and keep showing up together
a big crowd you see once a year at Christmas
a social club that meets in the parish hall

chat.says: what if i end up at a college where nobody's catholic? i just go solo, right?
options: Find two or three. Look up the campus Catholic group before you unpack.
Faith is between you and God; praying alone in your room is enough.
Wait a year till you're settled, then start looking for a church.
chat.meaning: Even the shut-door prayer says our. Two or three gathered in his name is enough, and the first Christians kept showing up together.

Matthew.meaning: the Gospel that gives the Our Father inside the Sermon on the Mount

Douay-Rheims.meaning: an older English Catholic translation of the Bible

Acts.meaning: the Acts of the Apostles, the story of the first Christians

apostles.meaning: the ones Jesus chose and sent out to teach

notes: Matthew 6:6, 18:20 and Acts 2:42 quoted from Douay-Rheims (Challoner); confirm exact wording.
'No I, no my' in the Our Father: checked against Douay-Rheims Matthew 6:9–13 (our, us, thy; no first person singular). Confirm.
'Faith is personal, never private' is a common Catholic phrasing (cf. CCC 166–167, 'faith is a personal act... not an isolated act'), voiced as 'Catholics put it this way'. Confirm the framing.
Original: κοινωνία (koinonia) as the Greek behind 'communication' in Acts 2:42 (DR); confirm.
